sub: Dumb questions, worse confessions — chaos that gets funnier.

1.name: Silly
q: Say the weirdest thing you've said to a pet — out loud, in the exact voice you used.~They rate how unhinged it was, out of ten.
On three, both name the smell you'd end a friendship over.~Then argue which is worse for thirty seconds.
Guess the thing I've been most confidently wrong about.~Then I tell you, and you say whether you'd have corrected me.
Describe your current mood using only kitchen appliances.~They have to guess the actual mood from it.
Which childhood toy was clearly designed to torment the adult in the room, not the kid?
Name the genre of your worst-decisions theme song, then hum four seconds of it.~They decide whether it has a key change.
Read out the strangest thing you've Googled convinced it was a medical emergency.~They diagnose you, badly.
Name a made-up rule you follow religiously.~They invent the punishment for breaking it. It applies all night.
You're a crisp flavour nobody asked for. Name it, pitch it in five seconds.~They decide whether they'd finish the bag.
Rank cereal, sandwiches and soup by how hard you'd fight for each.~They challenge one ranking. You defend it.
Make the sound that ends your entire mood.~They make theirs. Neither of you wins anything.
What's the strangest item you own that you also proudly display on a shelf?
Say a lie you told so long ago it's now load-bearing.~They ask two questions about it. Keep it consistent or it collapses.
Pitch your most delusional 'I could do that for a living' for thirty seconds.~They rate how close you got to convincing them.
Write your star sign's legally mandated warning label. Say it aloud.~Then they write yours, and theirs is the one that counts.
Reenact the most dramatic you've ever been in a supermarket.~They play the witness.
Do the fake injury you'd use to get out of a chore.~They rate whether they'd have bought it.
Say a word you use confidently with no idea what it means.~They get one guess at the real meaning. Then look it up.
Name the object you hold an irrational grudge against.~Now argue with it out loud for fifteen seconds.
Name your most useless talent — then perform it right now.~They score it out of ten.
Make the noise your soul makes when you sit down after a long day.~They try to match it. Better one wins.
Read out the most chaotic tab currently open on your phone.~No closing anything first.
Guess the skill I peaked at in primary school.~Then I demonstrate exactly how badly I've coasted.
What's a bad decision you've made that, honestly, given the chance again, you'd repeat?
Justify your least necessary purchase for thirty seconds, like you're in court.~They deliver the verdict.
What's a rule your family invented that you only recently realised isn't a universal law?
Reenact the most 'main character' you've felt over something tiny.~They rate the delusion out of ten.
Say the most unhinged thing you've said to Siri or a chatbot, in the same tone.~They reply as the chatbot.
What food combination do you secretly love that would end a first date if you ordered it in front of them?
Guess the most pathetic reason I've cried in public.~Then I tell you, and you rule on whether it was justified.
What's a smell that instantly turns you back into a nine-year-old?
Do the last lie you told a hairdresser, in the voice.~They play the hairdresser and press you on it.
Say a word you said wrong your whole life.~They get to use it correctly, pointedly, for the rest of the night.
Reenact the most chaotic thing you've done to win a board game.~They decide whether you should have been banned.
Do your go-to excuse for leaving a party early — on them, right now.~They rate how convincing it was.
What's a food you will physically defend on your plate, no negotiation?
Act out the weirdest thing you do when you're certain you're alone.~They guess what it is before you say.
Claim a skill you've lied about having. Now prove it, right now.~They rate the failure.
What's the most dramatic exit you've ever made from a group chat, a job, or bad Wi-Fi?
Pitch your low-stakes conspiracy theory for thirty seconds.~They argue against it, badly.
Reenact retrieving your phone from somewhere awful.~They narrate it like a nature documentary.
What's a childhood punishment you only now realise was wildly disproportionate to the crime?
Reenact your worst self-checkout argument. Both parts.~They judge who was right.
Perform the fake personality trait you kept up for a whole school year.~They guess what you were going for.
What's the pettiest thing you've ever returned or complained about, purely on principle?
What's a task you will always do the slow, hard way, purely out of stubbornness?
Act out how you avoid eye contact with someone you vaguely know.~They try it on you and see whether it works.

2.name: Absurd
q: You get cloned, but the clone only inherits your worst habits, maxed out. What's clone-you doing right now?
Everyone vote: who in this room becomes a cult leader first, and what's the cult actually about?
You're handed a parallel-universe version of yourself who made exactly one different choice, early on. What's different about their life?
Death shows up to collect you, but they're clearly new to the job and visibly nervous. Talk them through it.
Everyone vote: whose ghost would be the single most annoying one to get haunted by?
Your soul just received a formal, written customer complaint. Read us the opening line.
What's your hottest take about something almost everyone else in this room probably loves?
Would you rather sing every request you make for the rest of your life, or whisper every compliment you ever give again?
You wake up as the clearly-doomed side character in someone else's story. Whose story, and how do you go?
Everyone vote: who here is most likely to accidentally start a small war over something genuinely petty?
What's a secret society you would join purely, unapologetically, for the outfits?
Your evil twin exists somewhere and is, infuriatingly, doing better than you. What did they do differently?
Pitch the group your autobiography title, as written by someone who has personally had enough of you.
Would you rather your thoughts were subtitled live for everyone to read, or your inner monologue played on speaker for a week?
What's the worst possible thing to accidentally manifest into your actual life?
Everyone vote: who's getting recruited by aliens first — and are they going quietly?
What wellness trend are you convinced is just a cult with better branding?
You get one wish, but it's granted by a raccoon who resents you slightly. How does that go?
Your group chat gets subpoenaed. What's the one message that ends the whole case?
Would you rather know the exact date you die, or know exactly what everyone actually thinks of you, out loud, forever?
What's a genuinely terrible tattoo idea you would still, unfortunately, consider?
Pitch the worst possible theme park ride, and give it a name that would somehow still get approved.
What's the most chaotic possible thing to hear announced over a supermarket tannoy?
Everyone vote: who's most likely to fake their own disappearance and actually pull it off?
What's a hot take you have about how funerals, weddings, or birthdays are actually done wrong?
You've been legally assigned a government nemesis. What did you do to deserve one?
What's a completely made-up cosmic rule you're personally convinced governs the universe, zero evidence?
You're recruited into a support group for people who've all made the exact same specific mistake as you. What's the mistake, and who ends up running the group?
Everyone vote: who's most likely to join a pyramid scheme and defend it like a personality trait?
You wake up able to hear the thoughts of exactly one type of animal, forever. Which animal, and how fast do you regret it?
A stranger reads your browser history aloud at your funeral. What's the line that gets the audible gasp?
Would you rather be famous for a huge achievement nobody believes you actually did, or infamous forever for one small mistake everyone remembers perfectly?
You get a time machine that goes back exactly one week and lets you fix exactly one text message. Which one, and what did it nearly cost you?
Everyone vote: whose online reviews would be the most feared in this town?
A genie grants your wish, monkey's-paw style — technically true, catastrophically misread. What's the wish, and what's the catch?
You're the final boss in a video game based entirely on your own life. What's your attack pattern?
Everyone vote: who survives longest in a low-budget zombie movie, and who's dead in the first five minutes?
Your entire personality gets bottled and sold as a limited-edition soft drink. What's the flavour, and what's the health warning on the can?
Would you rather have a tiny, judgmental narrator following you everywhere, or a laugh track that plays after everything you say?
You're inducted into your town's Hall of Fame, but for something deeply unflattering. What does the plaque say?
Everyone vote: who sells out the group first for a genuinely small amount of money?
Would you rather everyone you meet instantly knew your most embarrassing memory, or instantly knew what you Googled last night?
You're granted the power to swap lives with anyone in this room for exactly 24 hours, no consent required. Who, and what do you immediately ruin?
Everyone vote: who's most likely to accidentally end up running a country they never meant to lead?
Pitch the worst possible spinoff of your own life — same universe, much worse main character.
You get to send younger-you exactly one item from the future, but it has to be something completely useless out of context. What is it, and why that?
Would you rather be legally required to narrate your own life out loud all day, or have everyone around you narrate it for you instead?

3.name: Unhinged
q: Guess the wildest thing I've done purely because I was bored.~Then I tell you, and you rate it out of ten.
Everyone vote, right now: who in this room ends up on a true-crime podcast — as the subject, not the host?
Deliver a eulogy for your own dignity. Cause of death — be specific.~The room decides whether it deserved a longer speech.
Leave the most deranged voicemail you can, right now, out loud.~They play it back as an impression.
The universe audits you. Say the line item it flags.~They add a second one you'd forgotten about.
Say the worst thing you've said the second someone left the room. No names.~They rate the crime out of ten.
Argue a position you know is wrong for thirty seconds, elaborately.~They name the exact point they nearly believed you.
You've died and you're being interviewed for your afterlife placement. What's the one answer that gets you sent somewhere worse?
Pitch your cult. One rule new members accept immediately, no negotiating.~They decide whether to join, and they have to answer.
Unlimited money, zero consequences, one hour. Narrate it live.~They interrupt once to make it worse.
Everyone vote: who cracks first under professional interrogation, and over what?
Do your impression of what your group chat sounds like to an outsider.~They rate how alarming it was.
Name a secret that would honestly just be a bit funny if it came out.~They guess how funny, out of ten. Then you tell them.
Reenact your most feral revenge over something genuinely small.~They rule on whether it was proportionate.
Say your most indefensible take.~They get thirty seconds to defend it better than you did.
Act out the most desperate move you've made to avoid admitting you were wrong.~They play the person you were arguing with.
Do the calm face you wore while causing complete chaos.~They guess the chaos.
Deliver your sock theory as a TED talk. Thirty seconds, full conviction.~They ask one hostile question at the end.
Whose villain era is happening right now, tonight, live, in this room?
Tell the darkest joke you know that's somehow still wholesome.~They rate the wholesomeness, not the darkness.
Say your worst 3am thought as a t-shirt slogan.~They design the back of the shirt.
Explain your entire personality using only your worst purchase.~They decide whether it holds up.
Would you rather everyone could hear your exact thoughts for one full day, or you had to say every thought out loud for one full hour?
Start a rumour about yourself right now that would actually spread.~They say whether they'd pass it on.
Everyone vote: who's most likely to talk their way out of an actual arrest on confidence alone?
Name the personal rule that's far too specific to explain.~They ask three questions until it makes sense. Or doesn't.
Reenact the smallest thing that ever made you briefly lose your mind.~They rate the overreaction.
Act out the most unhinged thing you've done to win an argument you didn't care about.~They play the other side.
Everyone vote: who in this room definitely has a secret second phone, and what's it for?
Five-years-ago you is blackmailing you. Say what they've got.~They set the ransom.
Say the most manipulative thing you've got away with.~They decide whether you should still feel bad. You accept the ruling.
Confess an event you were secretly relieved to get out of.~They guess the excuse you used.
Everyone vote: who in this room becomes genuinely dangerous the moment they get a little bit of power?
Say the cruellest private nickname you've given someone you still see.~They guess who it's for. You neither confirm nor deny.
Give the toast at your own roast — roast yourself, properly.~They add one line at the end, and it has to be worse.
Reenact the most calculated thing you did to be liked by someone undeserving.~They rate the effort against the payoff.
Everyone vote: whose search history would end the most friendships in this room, right now?
Name the grudge the other person has completely forgotten about.~They argue that person's case. You have to sit and listen.
Act out the most unhinged thing you've done purely for attention.~They decide whether they believe you'd deny it under oath.
Confess the worst thing you've done to avoid paying for something.~They rate the scheme out of ten for elegance.
Everyone vote: who has the most convincing "everything is fine" face while fully, quietly spiralling?
Narrate the opening scene of a documentary about your worst week.~They do the voiceover for scene two.
Say the most disturbing thing you learned about yourself secondhand.~They guess who told you.
Everyone vote: who's writing the tell-all book about this exact friend group, and who should be worried?
Name something you got away with and don't feel guilty about.~They decide whether you should. You take the verdict.
Reenact pretending you didn't break the expensive thing.~They play the person who found it.
Everyone vote: who's most likely to accidentally become a supervillain's origin story?

wild: Do a dramatic movie-trailer voiceover for whatever's happening in this room right now.
Do your best impression of the last person who genuinely annoyed you — no names, let the room guess who.
Announce the next round like a boxing ring announcer. Full volume, full drama, no exceptions.
Play both sides of a full-blown argument that started from one misread text message.
Give a slow-motion instant replay, with commentary, of the last clumsy thing you did today.
Strike a dramatic "I've just been betrayed" pose and hold it while the group invents increasingly ridiculous reasons why.
Pitch a fake perfume ad for how this exact moment, right now, smells.
Do your best impression of how you think you look dancing when you're sure no one's watching.
Deliver your next answer like a hostage negotiator gently talking everyone down.
Act out getting devastating news that turns out to be about something incredibly minor.
Do an impression of your own voicemail greeting — but the brutally honest version.
Whisper your next answer like it's classified information. Immediately deny you said anything.
Give the most dramatic possible reaction to someone else reaching for your food.
Do sixty seconds of stand-up about the single most annoying appliance in your home.
Give the most over-the-top motivational-speaker pep talk you can about doing absolutely nothing for the rest of tonight.
Answer the next question as your own evil twin — same facts, worst possible motives.
Give an Oscars acceptance speech for the most mundane thing you did today.
Narrate the next thirty seconds of this game like a hushed nature-documentary host.
Do your best impression of an infomercial host trying to sell this exact group chat to a stranger.
Deliver your next answer as a breaking-news anchor cutting live to a developing story.
Give a courtroom closing argument defending your worst decision from this past week.
Do an impression of the most unhinged automated customer-service voice you've ever dealt with.
Give the safety briefing for a flight that is very clearly about to go wrong.
Perform the most dramatic resignation speech you can over something tiny that happened five minutes ago.
final: Last one. Everyone silently picks the exact moment tonight you laughed the hardest.
On three, act it out again — badly, all at once, no context for anyone watching.
That's the one you'll actually remember. Go cause a better one.
